question_text: A system is best described as...
options: a single unchanging object
a list of unrelated facts
a set of connected parts with inputs and outputs
a model that is always correct in every situation

question_text: Negative feedback in a system...
options: removes the need for a model
reduces a change and helps keep conditions stable
increases a change without limit
prevents any input from ever entering the system at all

question_text: Positive feedback differs from negative feedback because it...
options: amplifies the original change
always makes a system stable
reduces all inputs to zero
only occurs in living organisms

question_text: Why do scientists use models?
options: To collect data without instruments
To replace all real experiments
To prove that a hypothesis is definitely true in every case
To simplify complex systems and make predictions

question_text: What is a key limitation of a scientific model?
options: It can never be changed once it is widely published
It contains no mathematics
It makes assumptions and ignores some factors
It always predicts the future exactly

question_text: Which practice most improves the reliability of a scientific claim?
options: Repeating the same error
Independent replication by other researchers
Publishing the work without any form of peer review
Using only one measurement

question_text: Two variables are strongly correlated. What can be concluded?
options: One may affect the other, but causation is not proved
The correlation must be accidental and cannot be explained
Both variables are independent
One variable definitely causes the other

question_text: What is needed to support a causal claim?
options: A mathematical coincidence
A single anecdote from a friend
A popular opinion poll of a very large number of people
A controlled experiment with suitable evidence

question_text: Scientific consensus is best described as...
options: a vote that cannot change
a theory with no evidence
the weight of evidence accepted by most experts
the opinion of one famous scientist who is on television

question_text: Risk is usually estimated from...
options: the age of the equipment being used
probability and severity of harm
cost and convenience only
public opinion alone

question_text: The precautionary principle suggests that...
options: action should be taken when serious harm is possible but uncertain
risk should always be ignored
no action is needed until harm has been proved beyond all possible scientific doubt
all new technology should be banned

question_text: A life cycle assessment evaluates...
options: the number of workers employed in every stage of production
the speed of a production line
the selling price of a product
environmental impacts from raw materials to disposal

question_text: A carbon footprint measures...
options: the number of vehicles owned
the area of land covered by trees and other plants
total greenhouse gases released by an activity
the amount of carbon in the soil

question_text: Which energy source is renewable?
options: Coal
Geothermal energy
Natural gas (methane)
Petroleum

question_text: A major challenge of solar and wind power is...
options: their output is intermittent
they produce no electricity
they cannot be scaled up
they release greenhouse gases

question_text: Sustainable development aims to...
options: use resources as quickly as possible
maximise economic growth at any cost to the environment
end all technological progress
meet present needs without harming future generations

question_text: Why is informed consent important in clinical trials?
options: It makes the trial cheaper to run
It guarantees that the treatment will work for everyone
Participants can decide freely whether to take part
It removes the need for controls

question_text: Randomisation in a clinical trial helps to...
options: remove all side effects
reduce bias between treatment groups
increase the dose given
guarantee a cure for every participant

question_text: Why is anonymisation used in health research?
options: To protect participants' personal privacy
To reduce the cost of the study
To allow data to be sold freely to companies
To make the results more accurate

question_text: Climate models show a range of future temperatures because...
options: scientists cannot agree on basic physics
the climate is completely random
all data are unreliable and cannot be used in any model
some factors are uncertain and models simplify reality

question_text: The ice-albedo feedback is an example of...
options: a system with no feedback
a closed system with no inputs
positive feedback that amplifies warming
negative feedback that strongly cools the entire planet

question_text: A circular economy attempts to...
options: discourage recycling
keep materials in use for as long as possible
increase the amount of single-use packaging in shops
maximise landfill waste

question_text: Why is international cooperation needed to tackle climate change?
options: Greenhouse gases affect the whole atmosphere
No country can act alone on energy
Climate data are owned by one nation
Every country has exactly identical emissions

question_text: Peer review is valuable because it...
options: guarantees that results are accurate and reliable
removes the need for replication
prevents all new ideas being shared
checks methods and evidence before publication
